FXHW60 PHFO 271358
AFDHFO

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Honolulu HI
358 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Moderate to locally breezy trades will occur through the 
remainder of the week. Stable and dry conditions will be the main  
theme the next several days. Typical summertime, albeit 
infrequent, windward and/or upslope mauka quick passing light 
showers. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Weak upper and mid level ridging across the Central Pacific
is providing just enough subsidence to result in warm and fairly 
dry weather, primarily isolated showers, the next couple of days.
A large area of 1032 mb surface high pressure located south of 
the Aleutian Islands is creating a tight enough pressure gradient 
toward lower equatorial pressure to create continued moderate to 
locally breezy trade winds the next several days. As was the case 
yesterday, the next few days will be less humid and generally 
more pleasant under continued moderate trade flow. 

The lower levels are void of any significant features that would 
indicate any short term deviation from the recent pattern. Morning
soundings indicate a near 6k ft inversion depth that is deep 
enough to support repeat showers. Locally stronger winds gusting 
to near 25 to 30 mph will be commonplace atop higher terrain and 
through lee valleys and/or slopes into early next week. Amped up 
trades will hang with us into early next week as subtle
strengthening of the North Pacific surface high puckers up winds
a touch past Sunday. Most diurnal rain accumulation will measure 
in the hundredths of an inch. Greater rainfall will likely focus 
across windward upslope areas, in particular Big Island's Hilo, 
Puna and Ka'u Districts and Haleakala's eastern slopes on Maui. 
Generally, as evidenced in recent soundings, mid to upper ridging 
will remain in control helping to maintain dry mid-levels (20-40% 
%RHs between 5-10k ft). This scenario will result in infrequent  
windward exposure showers. Quick-hitting light showers trapped 
within the trade belt will likely be more recurrent during the 
nocturnal hours than during the day. The rapid nature of these 
cells passing over high terrain will have better organized showers
wetting leeside communities. The weather pattern will turn more 
wet going into the middle of next week as deeper moisture reaches 
higher depths per weaker ridging slinking further west.

The National Hurricane Center is monitoring three distinct areas
of convection between 100W and 140W. All of these areas have a 
higher chance for tropical cyclone (TC) formation late this week 
or weekend. Deterministic model guidance has struggled with 
consistency on future development and track of potential TCs. 
Ensemble members that spin these eastern Pacific disturbances up 
into TCs and send them west are still in the minority. Google 
Deepmind is also struggling on how to handle the active convection
south of 14S between 130W and 140W this morning...NHC's area of a
high likelihood of TC formation. The model does send its ensemble
members of various strengths due west into a less sheared
environment south of the trade belt over Hawaii and over warmer 
waters through next week.

&&

.AVIATION...
Moderate trades expected through the period. Low cigs and SHRA 
over windward and mauka slopes. MVFR conds in heavier SHRA, 
otherwise VFR prevails.

AIRMET Tango is in effect for mod low-level turb lee of terrain
and may be needed for a few days.


&&

.MARINE...
Moderate to locally strong trades will persist through this
weekend as a broad high pressure remains far north of the state. 
A Small Craft Advisory for the typically windier waters around 
Maui County and the Big Island will continue through tonight and
likely need to be extended for the next several days. 

A small, long period south southwest swell will continue to fill 
in today, peak this tonight through Friday morning, then slowly 
fade through the weekend. This swell will help bump surf along 
south facing shores to above seasonal averages and could approach 
high surf criteria at its peak. 

Surf along east facing shores will remain rough and choppy due to
persistent trade wind swell. A small, medium period east swell
from Tropical Storm Iselle may fill in Friday, peak Saturday
before slowly fading into early next week. 

Surf along north facing shores will remain tiny to flat.


&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Dry regional air and moderate to locally breezy trade winds will 
maintain moderate fire weather concerns through the weekend. A 
slight increase in moisture early next week will only marginally 
improve conditions.


&&

.HFO WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
Small Craft Advisory until 6 AM HST Friday for Alenuihaha 
Channel-Big Island Leeward Waters-Big Island Southeast Waters-
Maalaea Bay-Pailolo Channel.


&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Blood
AVIATION...Walsh
MARINE...Thomas
